body_text:
A basis of a vector space $V$ over a field $F$ is a linearly
independent subset $B\subseteq V$ that spans $V$. Equivalently,
every vector of $V$ has a unique expression as a finite linear
combination of elements of $B$. The finiteness condition
applies to each combination even when the basis itself is
infinite.
